p2.en: There are two main treatments used by psychologists, namely, epithetic therapy, which focuses on developing an understanding of themselves and their problems, and behavioural therapy, which focuses on changing behaviour through conditionality.

p4.original: 心理学家采用的治疗方法主要有两种，即领悟疗法（侧重于发展对自身及其问题的理解）和行为疗法（侧重于通过条件作用来改变行为）。
p4.en: There are two main treatments used by psychologists, namely, epithetic therapy, which focuses on developing an understanding of themselves and their problems, and behavioural therapy, which focuses on changing behaviour through conditionality.

p5.original: 我们将看到，领悟疗法是最早被发展出来的真正的心理疗法，并且很长一段时间以来，它是唯一可用的心理疗法。近年来，领悟疗法已经与行为疗法相结合，并且行为疗法现已成为我们所拥有的最有效的工具（见图13-2）。但是，我们还是从领悟疗法开始讲起。
p5.en: We will see that epithetology is the first real psychotherapy to be developed and, for a long time, the only one available. In recent years, awareness therapy has been combined with behavioural therapy, which is now the most effective tool available to us (see figure 13-2). But let's start with the epithetology.

p14.original: 领悟疗法（insight therapy）试图改变人们的内在部分，即改变他们的思维和感受方式，有时也被称为谈话疗法。这些方法基于的假设是受困扰的人需要理解造成其精神困扰的不适宜的思维、情感以及动机。
p14.en: Insight therapy attempts to change the inner part of people, that is, the way they think and feel, sometimes called talking therapy. These approaches are based on the assumption that people in distress need to understand the inappropriate thinking, emotions and motivations that cause their mental distress.

p15.original: 领悟疗法约有数十种不同的“方法”（见图13-2），但是所有这些方法都旨在通过探讨和解释来揭示和改变患者充满困扰的心理过程。
p15.en: There are about dozens of different “methods” for epithets (see figure 13-2), but all of these methods are designed to reveal and change the troubled psychological processes of patients by exploring and interpreting them.

p16.original: 一些心理动力疗法，如弗洛伊德的精神分析，会假设问题隐藏在潜意识的深处，因此它们采用了精心设计和耗时的技术来挖掘出问题。
p16.en: Some psychodynamic therapy, such as Freud's psychoanalytical analysis, assume that the problem is hidden deep in the subconscious, so they use well-designed and time-consuming techniques to dig up the problem.

p17.original: 其他一些疗法，如卡尔·罗杰斯（Carl Rogers）的以来访者为中心的疗法，将无意识的重要性降至最低，通过让人们有意识地思考及在与他人的互动中寻找问题。在这里，我们只能列举一些最具有影响力的疗法，从西格蒙德·弗洛伊德开发出来的具有传奇色彩的心理疗法开始。
p17.en: Other treatments, such as Carl Rogers ' visitor-centred therapy, minimize the importance of unconsciousness by making people think and look for problems in their interactions with others. Here, we can cite only some of the most influential treatments, starting with the legendary psychotherapy developed by Sigmund Freud.

p21.original: 经典弗洛伊德学派的观点认为，心理问题源于不被允许的冲动和威胁性记忆在潜意识中产生的紧张感。因此，弗洛伊德疗法被正式称为精神分析（psychoanalysis），它对无意识状态进行了探究，以期将这些问题带入“现实”，也就是进入意识，使它们不再对个体造成伤害。因此，精神分析的主要目标是揭示和解释潜意识中的愿望、恐惧和欲望。
p21.en: According to the classic Freudian, psychological problems stem from an unpermissible impulse and a sense of subconscious stress arising from threatening memories. Thus, Freud therapy, officially known as psychoanalysis (psychoanalysis), explores the unconscious state with a view to bringing these problems into the “realities”, that is, into the consciousness, so that they do not cause harm to individuals. The main objective of psychoanalytical analysis is therefore to reveal and explain subconscious desires, fears and desires.

p22.original: 为了达到无意识层面，弗洛伊德寻求绕过自我（ego）为保护自己而建立的防御机制的方法。
p22.en: In order to reach the unconscious level, Freud sought ways to circumvent the defence mechanisms that he had set up to protect himself.

p23.original: 一种巧妙的方法叫作自由联想，通过这种方法，患者可以放松身心并谈论所想到的所有事情，治疗师则通过聆听并对涉及无意识需求和冲突的信息保持警惕。
p23.en: A clever approach called free association, whereby patients relax and talk about everything they think, and therapists listen and remain vigilant about information about unconscious needs and conflicts.

p24.original: 另一种方法叫作梦的解析，它依赖于患者梦中的象征性暗示。
p24.en: Another approach, called dream resolution, relies on symbolic intuitive in the patient's dream.

p25.original: 心理动力学疗法聚焦在来访者的动机上，无论是有意识的还是无意识的。这些观点都源自弗洛伊德。
p25.en: Psychodynamic therapy focuses on the motivations of visitors, be they conscious or unconscious. All of these points are drawn from Freud.

p26.original: 借助这些和其他技术，精神分析师会逐步发展出一个对问题的临床图像，并继续帮助患者了解其症状的无意识原因。为了让你对这一过程有所了解，下面我们来看一个关于弗洛伊德分析一名被诊断为“痴迷神经症”（在DSM-5中被诊断为强迫症）的19岁女孩的案例。请记住，即使弗洛伊德的观点已不再是心理学或精神病学的主流观点，但它们仍然很重要，因为其中的许多技术已被引入更新的治疗方法中。弗洛伊德的思想之所以重要，还因为他的许多概念，如自我、压抑、无意识、认同和俄狄浦斯情结（恋母情结），已经成为我们日常词汇的一部分。以下案例（你可能会发现弗洛伊德的解释令人震惊）会让你了解大约一个世纪前心理治疗的方式，并且这一方式至今仍然被一些正统的精神分析师采用。
p26.en: With these and other techniques, psychoanalysts will gradually develop a clinical image of the problem and continue to help patients understand the unintended causes of their symptoms. In order to give you an idea of the process, we will now look at the case of Freud analysing a 19-year-old girl who was diagnosed with “adult neurosis” (diagnosed as a compulsive disorder in DSM 5). Remember that even though Freud's point of view is no longer the mainstream of psychology or psychiatry, they are important, as many of these technologies have been introduced into the updated treatment. Freud's ideas are also important because many of his concepts, such as self, depression, unconsciousness, identity and Oedipus (honor love) have become part of our daily vocabulary. The following case (you may find Freud's explanation shocking) will make you aware of the way in which psychological care was administered about a century ago, and this is still being used by some orthodox psychoanalysts.

p27.original: 弗洛伊德解梦 弗洛伊德面对的这位“痴迷”患者每天晚上都要进行一个古怪的就寝仪式，这给她的父母带来了困扰。作为这种强迫性仪式的一部分，她首先关闭房间里的大钟，移走其他较小的时钟，包括她的手表。然后，她将所有花盆和花瓶都放在写字台上，因为以她的“神经症性”的思维方式，这样做后这些钟表在晚上就不会掉下来摔坏。然后，她在门口放置了各种物品，以保证房门保持半开的状态。在采取了这些预防措施之后，她又将注意力转移到床上，小心翼翼地确保枕头（厚枕头）不会碰到床头挡板，并且要求小枕头必须放在厚枕头对角线的中央。然后，她开始抖被子，直到里面所有羽绒都跑到被子的一角，再让它们均匀分布在被子里。之后她会爬到床上，把头放在枕头的正中间。
p27.en: Freud's dream of a strange sleeping ritual every night for the "love" patient Freud faces, which has troubled her parents. As part of this coercive ritual, she first closed the clock in the room and removed other smaller clocks, including her watch. She then placed all the flowerpots and vases on the desk because, in her “neurological” way of thinking, the clocks would not fall down at night. She then placed various items at the door to ensure that the door remained semi-open. After taking these precautions, she turned her attention to the bed, carefully ensuring that the pillow (the thick pillow) did not touch the bedhead shield and requiring that the small pillow must be placed in the centre of the thick pillow opposite the corner. Then she began to shake the covers until all the feathers in them ran to the corner of them, and spread them evenly among them. Then she climbs to the bed and puts her head in the middle of the pillow.

p28.original: 让这个个案的情况显得复杂的是，女孩永远没法确定自己是否已经正确地执行了仪式。在做完一遍后，她会再重复第一个步骤，然后再进行其他步骤——即使她向弗洛伊德承认，她在夜间采取的所有预防措施都是不合理的，但她每晚还是要花大约2个小时才能上床睡觉。
p28.en: The situation in this case is complicated by the fact that the girl will never be able to determine whether she has performed the ritual correctly. After that, she would repeat the first step and then take the other steps — even though she admitted to Freud that all the precautions she had taken at night were unreasonable, it would take her approximately two hours each night to go to bed.

p29.original: 在准备阅读弗洛伊德的解释之前，你可以考虑一下如何理解这一系列奇怪的行为。现在，看看用弗洛伊德（1920/1957）的精神分析对该个案的解释：
p29.en: Before preparing to read Freud's explanation, you can consider how to understand this strange set of behaviors. Now look at the interpretation of the case in the spirit of Freud (1920/1957):

p30.original: 病人逐渐了解到，她晚上在房间里搬动的这些钟表象征着女性的生殖器。我们知道，钟表除了具有其他象征意义外，还因其周期性过程和规则间隔的特点，也代表着生殖器官。我们可能会听到一个女人描述自己的月经就如同上了发条的钟表一样有规律。现在，这个病人特别担心的是钟表的嘀嗒声会影响她睡觉，此时钟表的嘀嗒声可能就像性兴奋一样。这种感觉让她感到很痛苦，实际上有好几次她因此从睡眠中醒来。为应对内心的恐惧，她采取了一种措施，即在夜间将所有的钟表移到离自己较远的地方。与所有容器的含义一样，花盆和花瓶也象征着女性的生殖器。因此，要采取预防措施防止它们在夜间掉落和摔碎……她对花盆和花瓶摔碎的预防措施表明，她对整个与童贞有关的危险都有抵触……
p30.en: The patient became aware that the clocks she moved in her room at night symbolized the female genitals. We know that the clock, among other symbolic features, also represents the genital organs because of the characteristics of its cyclical processes and rules. We might hear a woman describe her period as regular as a clock. Now, the patient is particularly worried about the sound of the clock, which affects her sleeping, as if it were sexual excitement. This feeling caused her pain, and in fact she woke up from sleep several times. In response to her inner fear, she took a measure to move all the clocks at night far away from her own. As with all containers, the flower basin and vases also symbolize female genitals. Therefore, precautions must be taken to prevent them from falling and falling at night... She has shown that she is in conflict with the whole danger associated with virginity...

p31.original: 有一天，她突然明白了自己的某个行为的含义，即不让厚枕头碰到床头挡板时，她开始把仪式的含义表达出来。她说，在她看来枕头就像女人，直立床头挡板是男人。因此，她希望通过一场魔法式的仪式可以把男人和女人分开。也就是说，要把父母分开，防止他们进行性交……
p31.en: One day, she suddenly understood the meaning of one of her acts, namely, that she would not allow a thick pillow to touch the bedhead, and she began to express the meaning of the ritual. She said that the pillow looked like a woman to her and that the bedhead was a man. She therefore hoped that men and women would be separated through a magical ritual. In other words, the parents should be separated and prevented from having sexual intercourse...

p32.original: 如果厚枕头代表着女人，那么抖动被子里的羽绒直到所有的羽绒都集中在一角鼓起，这也是有意义的。这意味着一个女人的受孕。尽管她把羽绒又抖开以避免怀孕，但还是无法忽略这件事，因为多年来她一直很害怕父母之间的性生活可能会带来另一个孩子并与她竞争。另一方面，如果厚枕头意味着母亲，那么小枕头就代表着女儿……因此，她自己则扮演了男人（父亲）的那部分，并用自己的头部代替了男性性器官。
p32.en: If the thick pillow represents a woman, it also makes sense to shake the feathers in the covers until all the feathers are concentrated in one corner. This means that a woman is pregnant. Although she shatters her feathers to avoid pregnancy, it is impossible to ignore this because for many years she has been afraid that the sexual life between her parents might bring another child and compete with her. On the other hand, if the thick pillow means the mother, the small pillow represents the daughter... So she herself plays the part of the man (father) and replaces the male sexual organ with her head.

p33.original: 你可能会说，一个女童的脑海中怎么会有这些可怕的想法。我承认这一点，但是不要忘了我并没有创造这些想法，只是揭露了它们……
p33.en: You might say how a girl can have these terrible thoughts in her head. I admit that, but don't forget that I didn't create these ideas, I just exposed them...

p34.original: 我们为你提供这种解释，不是因为我们希望你接受它，而是为了展示弗洛伊德是如何使用患者的症状作为象征性路标，进而指出潜在的和无意识的冲突、欲望和记忆的。但是，我们应该记住，弗洛伊德既是天才，又是他那个时代——维多利亚时代——的产物，当时的文化包含了矛盾的拘谨和对性的迷恋。人们出于含蓄，会将裤子套在他们的钢琴的“腿”（被认为是一个淘气的词）上，但与此同时，他们却被弗洛伊德的大胆理论吸引。关键是弗洛伊德显然将这种关于性的文化态度误认为是精神疾病的原因。
p34.en: We provide you with this explanation not because we want you to accept it, but to show how Freud used the symptoms of the patient as a symbolic signpost, pointing to potential and unconscious conflicts, desires and memories. But we should remember that Freud was both a genius and a product of his era — the Victorian era — when the culture was characterized by contradictory formalities and sexual obsessions. People, by implication, would put their pants on their piano “legs” (considered as a naughty word), but at the same time they were attracted to Freud's bold theory. The point is that Freud clearly misconstrues this cultural attitude about sexuality as the cause of mental illness.

p35.original: 精神分析治疗的过程 在治疗过程中，弗洛伊德帮助这个痴迷的年轻女孩了解她的自我防御机制（ego defense mechanism）如何将她的无意识问题转变为以性恐惧和性幻想为中心的强迫性就寝仪式。因此，通过替换这一自我防御机制，她把对失去童贞的恐惧变成了保护卧室里的花盆和花瓶的行为。这样她的自我就满足了她的潜意识需求。同时，它可以通过另一种被称为压抑（repression）的防御机制，使“实际”问题不受意识的影响。
p35.en: In the process of psychoanalytic therapy, Freud helped this obsessed young girl to understand how her self-defense mechanisms turned her unconscious problems into forced sleeping rituals centred on sexual fear and fantasies. As a result, by replacing this self-defence mechanism, she has turned the fear of losing her virginity into an act of protecting the flower pots and vases in her bedroom. So that her self meets her subconscious needs. At the same time, it can shield “real” issues from conscious influence through another defence mechanism known as repression.

p36.original: 因此，一个正统的弗洛伊德式精神分析师的主要任务是帮助患者突破压抑的阻碍，并将具有威胁性的想法带入意识。通过这一做法，患者可以洞悉当前症状和所抑制的冲突之间的关系。弗洛伊德认为，当患者开始理解并接受这些无意识的冲突和欲望时，它们就不会再引发麻烦。
p36.en: Thus, the main task of an orthodox Freudian psychoanalyst is to help patients break through the depressing obstacles and to bring threatening ideas into the consciousness. Through this practice, patients can discover the relationship between the current symptoms and the conflicts that are being suppressed. Freud believes that when patients begin to understand and accept these unintentional conflicts and desires, they do not cause any further trouble.

p37.original: 最终，在精神分析的最后阶段，患者会了解他们与治疗师建立的关系如何反映了未解决的冲突，尤其是与父母之间的问题。这种把对父母的反应投射在治疗师身上的情况被称为移情，因此治疗的最后阶段被称为移情分析（analysis of transference）。根据精神分析理论，康复的最后一步是，患者最终摆脱了孩童时期与在父母的关系中建立的无意识障碍（Munroe，1955）。
p37.en: Ultimately, in the final stages of psychoanalysis, patients will learn how their relationship with the therapist reflects unresolved conflicts, especially with their parents. This projection of reactions to parents to therapists is called a diversion, and the final phase of treatment is therefore called a transient analysis (analysis of treatment). According to the psychoanalytical theory, the last step in rehabilitation is that the patient eventually emerges from the unconscious barriers that were created in childhood in the relationship with his parents (Munroe, 1955).

p38.original: 西格蒙德·弗洛伊德的书房，包括著名的躺椅（右），位于伦敦的弗洛伊德博物馆中。82岁的弗洛伊德在纳粹占领奥地利后于1938年逃往伦敦，并于次年在伦敦去世。
p38.en: Sigmund Freud's library, including the famous recital chair (right), is located at the Freud Museum in London. Freud, 82 years old, fled to London in 1938 after the Nazi occupation of Austria and died the following year in London.

p39.original: 13.3.2 新弗洛伊德主义心理动力学疗法

p40.original: 请允许本书作者对弗洛伊德也做一些分析：很明显他具有戏剧天赋，而且他还拥有强大的、充满魅力的个性，或者正如他本人曾经说的那样，拥有强大的自我。因此，弗洛伊德鼓励他的学生们对精神分析原理进行辩论，但他不能容忍他们对他的学说进行根本性改变。这导致了他与和他意志同样坚强的一些追随者之间不可避免的冲突，如阿尔弗雷德·阿德勒、卡尔·荣格和卡伦·霍妮，他们最终与弗洛伊德分道扬镳并建立了自己的治疗理论。
p40.en: Please allow the author of this book to make some analysis of Freud: it is clear that he has a dramatic talent and that he also has a strong, charismatic personality or, as he himself once said, a strong self. Freud therefore encouraged his students to debate the principles of psychoanalysis, but he could not tolerate a fundamental change in his doctrine. This led to an inevitable conflict between him and some of his followers who were as strong as his will, such as Alfred Adler, Karl Jung and Karen Horne, who eventually split up with Floyd and established their own therapeutic theory.

p41.original: 总体而言，这些心理动力学理论着重于无意识的动机和情感困扰。从形式上讲，新弗洛伊德主义倡导者保留了弗洛伊德的许多基本思想和技术，同时也增加并修改了一些观点和方法。在真正的心理动力学传统中，新弗洛伊德主义心理动力学疗法（neo-Freudian psychodynamic therapy）保留了弗洛伊德对动机的重视。现在，大多数精神分析师已经摒弃了躺椅，开始面对面地治疗患者。并且大多数精神分析师会在几个月内每周与患者见一次面，而不像传统精神分析治疗那样在几年内一周见好几次面。
p41.en: Overall, these psychodynamic theories focus on unconscious motivations and emotional distress. Formally, the neo-Freudist advocates retained many of Freud's basic ideas and techniques, while adding and modifying some ideas and approaches. In the true tradition of psychodynamics, Neo-Freudian psychodynamics (neo-Freudian psychodynamic therapy) retained the importance that Freud attached to motivation. Now, most psychoanalysts have abandoned their recital chairs and have begun to treat patients face to face. Moreover, most psychoanalysts meet with patients once a week in a few months, rather than several times a week in a few years, as is the case with traditional psychoanalytic treatment.

p42.original: 那么你如何看待现代心理动力学治疗师在更短的时间内完成治疗工作呢？
p42.en: So what do you think of modern psychodynamic therapists completing treatment in a shorter time?

p43.original: 他们中的大多数将重点转移到了有意识的动机上，因此没有花太多时间在潜意识中寻找隐藏的冲突和被压抑的记忆。大多数人还通过强调以下一项或多项观点以与弗洛伊德有所区别：
p43.en: Most of them have shifted their focus to conscious motivations, so that they have not spent much time in subconscious search for hidden conflicts and repressed memories. Most of them also distinguished themselves from Freud by emphasizing one or more of the following points:

p44.original: 有意识的自体或自我（而不是本我）的意义；
p44.en: The meaning of conscious self or self (and not of myself)

p45.original: 整个一生中经历的影响（与弗洛伊德强调早期的经历相反）；
p45.en: Impacts experienced throughout the life cycle (in contrast to Freud's emphasis on early experiences);

p46.original: 社会需求和人际关系的作用（而非性驱力和攻击性驱力）。
p46.en: The role of social needs and relationships (rather than sexual and offensive).

p47.original: 每一个新弗洛伊德主义理论家都建立了一种关于障碍和治疗的理论，但各自强调的重点有所不同。在这里我们无法更详细地介绍这些方法，但我们可以简要地描述一下现代心理动力学治疗师如何处理弗洛伊德描述的强迫症女孩的情况。这些治疗师很可能会关注当前女孩与父母之间的关系，也许会关注她是否在借每天晚上两个小时的强迫仪式成为父母关注的焦点，以弥补自己对这种关系的不满足感。而且，治疗师可能不会对女孩进行如此频繁的治疗，而是会与其父母一起改变他们处理问题的方式。为了进一步说明这一点，在本章开始时我们遇到了心情沮丧的德里克，那么对此这些治疗师该如何进行治疗呢？尽管一位正统的弗洛伊德式分析师将探究他关于童年的记忆以寻找其患抑郁症的线索，但现代的心理动力学治疗师将更可能在其目前的关系中寻找线索，并假设原因是社会关系而非性关系。
p47.en: Every new Freudist theorist has developed a theory of barriers and treatment, but each has a different emphasis. We cannot describe these methods in more detail here, but we can briefly describe how modern psychokinetic therapists deal with the girl with the stress disorder described by Freud. These therapists are likely to focus on the relationship between the girl and her parents at present, and perhaps on whether she is focusing on her parents ' concerns through a forced ritual of two hours a night to compensate for her dissatisfaction with the relationship. Moreover, the therapists may not treat girls so frequently, but rather change the way they deal with the problems with their parents. To illustrate this point further, at the beginning of this chapter we met with the depressed Derek, and how should these therapists treat it? While a orthodox Freudian analyst will explore his childhood memory to find clues to his depression, modern psychodynamic therapists will be more likely to find clues in their current relationships, assuming that they are due to social rather than sexual relationships.

p49.original: 与强调动机冲突的心理动力学不同，人本主义治疗师认为，心理问题源于低自尊、目标被误导和不完美的关系。的确，寻求治疗的大学生的主要症状包括疏离感、无法实现他们认为应该实现的目标、糟糕的人际关系以及对生活的普遍不满意。治疗师经常将上述提到的日常生活中存在的问题称为存在危机，这个术语强调了人类面临的许多问题是关于一个人存在的意义和目的。人本主义心理学家已经发展出专门针对此类问题的疗法。
p49.en: Unlike psychokinetics, which emphasize the conflict of motivations, humanist therapists believe that psychological problems stem from low self-esteem, misguided targets and imperfect relationships. Indeed, the main symptoms of university students seeking treatment include a sense of alienation, failure to achieve what they believe should be achieved, poor interpersonal relations and general dissatisfaction with life. The term " crisis ", often referred to by therapists as the problems of everyday life referred to above, emphasizes the significance and purpose of many of the problems faced by humanity in relation to the existence of a person. Humanist psychologists have developed treatments specifically designed for such problems.

p50.original: 人本主义治疗师通常会帮助来访者应对低自尊、糟糕的人际关系以及存在危机。
p50.en: Humanist therapists often help visitors cope with low self-esteem, poor interpersonal relations and crises.

p51.original: 与心理动力学治疗师的观点相反，人本主义治疗师认为，人们经常受到成长和心理幸福这一健康需求的激励。他们对弗洛伊德关于将人格划分为相互冲突的部分的假设提出异议，这种人格由自私的本我主导，由享乐主义的本能和被压抑的冲突所驱动。取而代之的是，人本主义心理学家强调不断发展和变化的全人概念。
p51.en: Contrary to the point of view of psychodynamic therapists, humanist therapists believe that people are often motivated by the health needs of growth and psychosocial well-being. They challenged Freud's assumption that he would divide personality into conflicting parts, dominated by selfish me, driven by the instincts of hedonism and repressed conflict. Instead, humanist psychologists emphasize the concept of the human being as a whole as it evolves and changes.

p52.original: 人本主义心理学家认为，当个体正常的发展受到干扰并产生低自尊时，就会导致精神障碍。因此，人本主义疗法（humanistic therapy）试图通过承认来访者是自由的，增强他们的自尊心并实现其最大的潜能来帮助他们应对问题（Schneider & May，1995）。一位人本主义治疗师（如果大约在一个世纪前就已经存在）可能会与弗洛伊德的强迫症患者一起研究她的自我概念和对父母的感受。至于德里克，人本主义治疗师可能会猜测，他的抑郁是由于不满意的人际关系或个人能力不足造成的。
p52.en: Humanistic psychologists believe that when the normal development of an individual is disrupted and low self-esteem is generated, mental disorders arise. Humanist therapy therefore seeks to help visitors to cope by recognizing them as free, enhancing their self-esteem and realizing their maximum potential (Schneider & May, 1995). A humanist healer (if it already existed about a century ago) could work with Freud's coercive patients to study her self-perception and feelings for her parents. As for Derek, the humanist therapist might speculate that his depression was caused by unsatisfactory interpersonal relationships or insufficient personal abilities.

p53.original: 来访者中心疗法 来访者中心疗法（client-centered therapy）也许是人本主义疗法中被使用最广泛的一种方法，是由传奇人物卡尔·罗杰斯（Carl Rogers，1951，1977）发展出来的。这一方法假设一个对积极自我形象的渴望与来自自我和他人的批评之间的冲突会破坏人的健康发展。这种冲突造成了焦虑和不愉快。为此，罗杰斯的以来访者为中心疗法的任务就是创造一个滋养性的环境，使人们可以在这种环境中解决自己的困扰，并最终提升自尊和自我实现。
p53.en: Visitor center therapy The visitor center therapy, perhaps the most widely used method of humanist therapy, was developed by legendary Carl Rogers, 1951, 1977. This approach assumes that a conflict between a desire for a positive self-image and criticism from self and others can undermine the healthy development of people. This conflict has caused anxiety and discomfort. To this end, Rogers ' mission of visitors-centred therapy is to create a nurturing environment in which people can address their own problems and ultimately enhance their self-esteem and self-fulfilment.

p54.original: 罗杰斯学派治疗师使用的主要技术之一是情感反映（reflection of feeling，又称反应性倾听），以帮助来访者理解他们的情绪。通过这种技术，治疗师释义来访者的话语，充当一种心理“镜子”，来访者可以从中看到自己。在以下来访者中心治疗过程的摘录中，请注意治疗师是如何使用这项技术来捕捉一名年轻女子表达出来的情绪的（Rogers，1951）。
p54.en: One of the main techniques used by Rogers school therapists is emotional response (also known as reactive listening) to help visitors understand their emotions. Through this technique, the therapist interprets the words of visitors, acting as a psychological “morror”, from which visitors can see themselves. In the following excerpt of the treatment process at the Visitors Centre, attention is drawn to how the therapist used this technique to capture the emotions expressed by a young woman (Rogers, 1951).

p55.original: 来访者：这可能一直追溯到我的童年……母亲告诉我，我是父亲的宠儿。尽管我从来没有意识到这一点——我的意思是，他们从来就没有宠过我。而且其他人似乎总觉得我在这家里是一个有特权的孩子……现在我回过头来看，这只是家庭让其他孩子能更多地逃避惩罚的原因，而出于其他某种原因，他们似乎对我比其他孩子更严格。
p55.en: Visitor: This may have been going back to my childhood... and my mother told me that I was a father's pet. Although I never realized that -- I mean, they never spoiled me. And others seem to think that I'm a privileged child in this house... Now I look back and see that it's just why the family lets other children escape punishment more, and for some other reason they seem to be tougher on me than on other children.

p56.original: 治疗师：无论从哪个方面，你都无法感受到来自父母的宠爱，而家庭状况似乎也对你提出了更高的标准。
p56.en: Therapeutician: In any respect, you cannot feel the love of your parents, and family conditions seem to set a higher standard for you.

p57.original: 来访者：嗯。这就是我面对的一切，并且其他人可以犯错，或者像个顽皮的孩子一样捣蛋……但爱丽丝不能那样做。
p57.en: Visitor: Hmm. And that's all I'm dealing with, and others can make mistakes, or mess with it like a naughty kid but Alice can't do that.

p58.original: 治疗师：嗯。其他人那样做只是有点顽皮。但对你而言，就不应该这样做。
p58.en: Therapist: Hmm. Others just do it a little naughty. But for you, that is not the case.

p59.original: 来访者：这确实是我的想法。我认为父母对我的标准……是一个我需要咨询和思考的问题，因为我一直在怀疑是否有人真诚地对待过我。
p59.en: Visitor: It was really my idea. I think that the standard of parents for me is a question of advice and reflection, because I have been wondering if anyone has treated me in good faith.

p60.original: 治疗师：嗯。你现在无法确定自己是否有更深的价值感。
p60.en: Therapist: Hmm. You're not sure if you have a deeper sense of value.

p62.original: 请注意，在此示例中，治疗师的大多数陈述是在释义或“反映”来访者刚刚说的话。
p62.en: Please note that, in this example, most of the therapist's statements are interpreted or “reflected” what the visitor has just said.

p63.original: 这一方法有效吗？实际上，来访者中心疗法拥有大量的科学研究支持。美国心理学会一个特别工作组负责寻找能够支持治疗有效性的科学实践，结果发现有效的治疗方法拥有的共同因素，恰恰是罗杰斯学派的同理心、积极关注、真诚和反馈（Ackerman et al.，2001）。
p63.en: Is this method working? In fact, the visitors ' centre therapy is heavily supported by scientific research. A task force of the American Psychological Association, which seeks out scientific practices that support treatment effectiveness, has found common elements of effective treatment, precisely the same sense, positive concern, sincerity and feedback of Rogers (Ackerman et al., 2001).

p65.original: 到目前为止，我们已经讨论的领悟疗法主要关注人们的情绪或动机。
p65.en: So far, the awareness therapy that we have been discussing has focused primarily on people's emotions or motivations.

p66.original: 另一方面，认知疗法（cognitive therapy）假设心理问题源于错误的思维，并将理性思维视为积极治疗和改变的关键（Butler et al.，2006）。认知疗法有很多形式，但在这里我们只举一个例子来说明：亚伦·贝克（Aaron Beck）用认知疗法来治疗抑郁症。
p66.en: On the other hand, cognition therapy assumes that psychological problems stem from erroneous thinking and considers rational thinking as the key to positive treatment and change (Butler et al., 2006). Cognitive therapy takes many forms, but here we can just give one example: Aaron Beck uses cognitive therapy to treat depression.

p67.original: 认知疗法的重点是改变来访者对自己和世界的看法。
p67.en: The focus of cognitive therapy is on changing visitors ' perceptions of themselves and the world.

p68.original: 贝克最初接受的是经典精神分析的培训，但后来他注意到他的抑郁症患者的梦和自由联想充满了消极的想法，于是他开始打破弗洛伊德的传统（Beck，1976；Bowles，2004）。通常，患者们会发表自嘲的言论，如“如果他们真的了解我，就没人会喜欢我”和“我不太聪明，无法在竞争这么激烈的学校里表现出色”。贝克逐渐确信，是这种消极的自我对话导致人们抑郁。所以，治疗师的工作就是帮助来访者学习更多的积极思维方式。
p68.en: Baker was initially trained in classical psychoanalysis, but later noted that his depression patients' dreams and free association were filled with negative ideas, and he began to break Freud's tradition (Beck, 1976); Bowles, 2004. Usually, patients make scornful statements, such as “If they really know me, no one will like me” and “I'm not very smart enough to perform in such competitive schools”. Baker became convinced that this negative self-dialogue led to depression. So it's the job of the therapist to help visitors learn more positive ways of thinking.

p69.original: 以下是贝克的治疗方法的示例，摘自与德里克年龄相仿的一名大学生进行的一次治疗的对话（Beck et al，1979）。
p69.en: The following is an example of Baker's treatment, taken from a conversation with a university student of the same age as Derek (Beck et al., 1979).

p70.original: 来访者：当事情出错时我会感到沮丧。就像我考试不及格一样。
p70.en: Visitor: I'm frustrated when things go wrong. Just like I failed the exam.

p71.original: 治疗师：考试不及格为何会使你感到沮丧？
p71.en: Therapists: Why do you feel frustrated by failing the exams?

p72.original: 来访者：好吧，如果我考试失败，就永远也不能上法学院了。
p72.en: Visitors: Well, if I fail, I'll never go to law school.

p73.original: 治疗师：你是否同意你解释考试结果的方式会影响你？你可能会感到沮丧、无法入睡、食欲不振，甚至可能会怀疑是否该放弃这门功课。
p73.en: Therapist: Do you agree that the manner in which you explain the results of the examination will affect you? You may feel frustrated, be unable to sleep, suffer from hunger, or even doubt whether you should give up your homework.

p74.original: 来访者：是的，我同意。我一直在想我不会成功。
p74.en: Visitors: Yes, I agree. I keep thinking I won't succeed.

p75.original: 治疗师：现在考试失败意味着什么？
p75.en: Therapist: What does failure mean now?

p76.original: 来访者：（泪流满面）我无法进入法学院。
p76.en: Visitor: I can't get into law school.

p77.original: 治疗师：那对你意味着什么？来访者：我不够聪明。
p77.en: Therapist: What does that mean to you? Visitor: I'm not smart enough.

p79.original: 来访者：我永远都不会开心。
p79.en: Visitor: I will never be happy.

p80.original: 治疗师：这些想法会让你感到怎样？
p80.en: Therapist: How do you feel about these ideas?

p82.original: 治疗师：因此，考试不及格的意义是会让你很不开心。实际上，相信自己永远无法开心是造成你不开心的重要因素。因为，你掉进了一个陷阱里——它的定义是，不能进入法学院等于“我永远不会开心”。
p82.en: The therapist: So the point of failure is to make you unhappy. In fact, believing that you can never be happy is a major factor in your displeasure. Because you fell into a trap -- it was defined as, "I will never be happy" without going to law school.

p83.original: 从上述交流中我们可以看出，认知治疗师可以帮助人们直面破坏性思维来改善抑郁症状。研究表明，在治疗抑郁症方面，贝克的方法至少可以和药物一样有效（Antonuccio，1995；Beck，2005）。
p83.en: From the above exchanges, we can see that cognitive therapists can help people face destructive thinking to improve depression. Studies have shown that Baker's approach can be at least as effective as medication in treating depression (Antonuccio, 1995); Beck, 2005.

p84.original: 在德里克这个个案中，认知治疗师无疑会寻找可能使他抑郁的消极自我对话。
p84.en: In the case of Derek, the cognitive therapist will undoubtedly look for negative self-dialogues that may cause him to be depressed.

p85.original: 认知治疗师会如何面对弗洛伊德的那位19岁的强迫症患者？他们会把重点放在患者非理性的信念上，如花盆和花瓶可能会在晚上会掉下来摔坏的想法。认知治疗师还会挑战来访者的假设，即如果她不遵守睡前仪式，可能会发生灾难性事件（如无法入睡）。在这两种情况下，认知治疗师做出的假设是，症状会随着积极思维取代消极思维而消失。
p85.en: How does a cognitive therapist confront the 19-year-old compulsive patient of Freud? They will focus on the irrational beliefs of patients, such as the idea that a flower pot and vase may fall down at night. Cognitive therapists also challenge visitors ' assumptions that if they do not observe the pre-sleep ritual, catastrophic events (e.g. if they cannot sleep) may occur. In both cases, cognitive therapists assume that symptoms disappear as positive thinking replaces negative thinking.

p87.original: 截止到现在，我们所讨论的治疗方法一般都涉及患者或来访者与治疗师之间的一对一关系。但是，大多数情况下也可以由两人或更多人组成的治疗小组来完成。在处理人际关系方面的困扰时，这种团体治疗（group therapy）比个体治疗更有优势。事实上，团体治疗通常会成为涉及夫妻、家庭或其他具有类似问题（如抑郁症或吸毒成瘾）的群体寻求治疗时的首选方法。
p87.en: As of now, the treatment we are discussing generally involves a one-to-one relationship between the patient or visitor and the therapist. In most cases, however, treatment teams of two or more persons could also be used. When dealing with interpersonal distress, group therapy is more advantageous than individual treatment. In fact, group therapy is often the preferred method of seeking treatment involving couples, families or other groups with similar problems, such as depression or addiction.

p88.original: 虽然有些团体会尝试线上治疗，但通常治疗团体每周会面一次（Davison et al，2000）。在许多情况下，尽管心理动力学和认知行为视角的治疗团体也很普遍，但团体治疗师大多还是采用人本主义的视角。无论采用哪种方法，团体治疗都可以为患者提供在宽容和支持的环境下观察和模仿新的社会行为的机会。为了简洁起见，接下来我们将仅讨论两种代表性的团体治疗：自助支持团体、婚姻与家庭疗法。
p88.en: Although some groups try on-line treatment, treatment groups usually meet once a week (Davison et al., 2000). In many cases, group therapists have largely adopted a humanistic perspective, although therapeutic groups with psychodynamic and cognitive behavioural perspectives are common. In either way, group therapy provides patients with the opportunity to observe and imitate new social behaviours in a tolerant and supportive environment. For the sake of brevity, we will then discuss only two representative group treatments: self-help support groups, and marriage and family therapy.

p89.original: 虽然从业者采用团体治疗的角度不同，但他们都利用了团体的社会环境。
p89.en: Although practitioners have different perspectives on group therapy, they have all taken advantage of the group's social environment.

p90.original: 自助支持团体 在团体治疗中，最值得关注的也许就是人们对自助支持团体（self-help support groups）的兴趣激增。目前存在成千上万个这样的团体，许多都是免费的，特别是那些不是由付费医疗专业人员指导的团体。这样的团体使人们有机会在不受威胁的条件下会面，与有类似问题的其他人交流想法，这些人有的已经摆脱困扰，有的甚至取得了非凡的成就（Schiff & Bargal，2000）。
p90.en: Self-help support groups are perhaps the most interesting group treatments where there is a surge in interest in self-help support groups. There are thousands of such groups, many of which are free of charge, especially those not directed by paid medical professionals. Such groups provide an opportunity to meet without threats and exchange ideas with others with similar problems, some of whom have emerged from their troubles and have achieved extraordinary achievements (Schiff & Bargal, 2000).

p91.original: 最早的支持团体戒酒互助会（Alcoholics Anonymous，AA）于20世纪30年代中期开始倡导自助的概念。最初AA的核心是戒除酒瘾的12个步骤。需要注意的是，这12个步骤并非基于心理学理论，而是基于早期AA成员反复试验的结果。
p91.en: Alcoholics Anonymous, AA, the first support group, started advocating the concept of self-help in the mid-1930s. At the heart of the AA was the 12 steps to stop alcohol addiction. It is important to note that these 12 steps are not based on psychological theory but rather on the results of repeated trials by early AA members.

p92.original: 到了20世纪60年代，女权主义者意识提升运动使更多的民众了解了自助这一概念。现在出现了许多解决各种问题的自助支持团体，其中包括：
p92.en: By the 1960s, feminist awareness-raising campaigns had made the concept of self-help known to a wider audience. A number of self-help support groups have emerged to address various issues, including:

p93.original: 处理生活转变或其他危机，如离婚或孩子的死亡；
p93.en: Dealing with changes in life or other crises, such as divorce or the death of a child;

p94.original: 应对身体和精神障碍，如心脏病或抑郁症；
p94.en: Addressing physical and mental disorders, such as heart disease or depression;

p95.original: 处理成瘾和其他不受控制的行为，如酗酒、赌博、暴饮暴食、纵欲过度和药物依赖；
p95.en: (b) Dealing with addiction and other uncontrolled behaviours, such as alcohol abuse, gambling, drinking and consumption, over-alcoholism and drug dependence;

p96.original: 处理成瘾者的亲戚或朋友感受到的压力。
p96.en: The pressure felt by relatives or friends dealing with addicts.

p97.original: 团体治疗也为绝症患者的治疗做出了宝贵的贡献。这种治疗的目的是帮助患者及其家人尽可能活得好一些，切实应对即将到来的死亡，并适应患病晚期的身体病痛。这类身患绝症的支持团体的重点是帮助患者学习“如何充实地活着直到说再见”（Nungesser，1990）。
p97.en: Group therapy also makes a valuable contribution to the treatment of terminally ill people. The aim of such treatment is to help patients and their families to live as well as possible, to respond effectively to imminent deaths and to adapt to advanced physical pains. The focus of these terminally ill support groups is to help patients learn “how to live well until they say goodbye” (Nungesser, 1990).

p98.original: 婚姻与家庭疗法 与那些正在为关系而苦苦挣扎的人们一起工作也许是了解关系最好的环境。例如，夫妻治疗（或咨询）可能涉及一对夫妻，他们正在学习并弄清他们的交流方式并提高互动的质量（Napier，2000）。通过为一对夫妻（通常一次只有一对）提供咨询，治疗师可以帮助他们确定他们之间的沟通风格，是支配、控制或混淆彼此的言语，还是非言语沟通（Gottman，1994，1999）。然后，治疗师可以帮助他们巩固彼此之间更理想的反应模式并减少冲突。夫妻通常会学习一些非指导性倾听技巧，这些技巧有助于澄清和表达感受以及想法，而不会产生对抗（Jacobson et al，2000；Wheeler et al，2001）。
p98.en: Marriage and family therapy, working with people who are struggling to get along with each other, is probably the best environment to understand relationships. For example, spousal therapy (or counselling) may involve a couple who is learning and understanding how they communicate and improving the quality of their interactions (Napier, 2000). By providing advice to a couple (usually only one at a time), the therapist can help them determine the style of communication between them, whether to dominate, control or confuse each other's words or to communicate in a non-verbal manner (Gottman, 1994, 1999). The therapists can then help them to consolidate a more desirable pattern of response among themselves and to reduce conflict. Spouses usually learn non-directive listening techniques that help clarify and express feelings and ideas without confrontation (Jacobson et al., 2000); Wheeler et al., 2001.

p99.original: 在夫妻治疗中，治疗师可以帮助夫妻一起努力改善彼此已经形成的沟通方式。
p99.en: In the case of spousal treatment, the therapist can help the couple to work together to improve the way they communicate with each other.

p100.original: 在家庭治疗中，“服务对象”是整个家庭群体，每个家庭成员都被视为关系系统的一部分（Fishman，1993）。家庭治疗师可以帮助陷入困境的家庭成员感知给他们带来麻烦的问题或模式。家庭治疗的目的是改变参与者之间的人际动态（互动）（Foley，1979；Schwebel & Fine，1994）。家庭治疗不仅有助于减轻家庭内部的紧张感，而且还可以通过帮助单个家庭成员认识到他们在团体中的作用，并更好地提高这种作用。它已经被证明可以有效地治疗神经性厌食症、抑郁症和其他心境障碍，甚至可以为患有精神分裂症的家庭带来帮助（Miklowitz，2007）。
p100.en: In family therapy, the “client” is the whole family group, and each family member is considered part of the relationship system (Fishman, 1993). Family therapists can help family members in distress to feel the problems or patterns that cause them trouble. Family therapy aims to change the interpersonal dynamics (interactivity) among participants (Foley, 1979); Schwebel & Fine, 1994. Family therapy not only helps to reduce tension within the family, but also helps individual family members to recognize and better enhance their role in the group. It has proved effective in treating neuro anorexia, depression and other mental disorders, and can even help families with schizophrenia (Miklowitz, 2007).

p102.original: 心理动力学疗法与认知疗法

p103.original: 你认为心理动力学疗法和认知疗法之间的主要区别是什么？
p103.en: What do you think is the main difference between psychodynamic and cognitive therapy?

p106.original: 了解目前使用的行为疗法的主要方式。
p106.en: To understand the main ways in which behavioural therapy is currently used.

p107.original: 如果来访者的问题是暴饮暴食、尿床、羞怯、反社会行为或可以用纯行为学术语描述的其他任何障碍，都有可能通过某种行为疗法（也称行为矫正）对其进行调整。行为疗法（behavior therapy）的假设是，不良行为是习得的，因而也可以通过学习消除，它依赖于操作性条件反射和经典条件反射的原则（见图13-2）。除了先前列出的那些困难之外，行为治疗师还报告说他们成功地应对了恐惧、强迫、抑郁、成瘾、攻击性和违法行为。
p107.en: If the visitors ' problems are severe drinking, bed wetting, shyness, antisocial behaviour or any other barrier that can be described in pure behavioural terms, it is possible to adjust them through some form of behavioural therapy (also known as behavioural correction). Behavior therapy is based on the assumption that bad behaviour is acquired and can therefore be eliminated through learning, and relies on the principles of operational and classical conditions reflection (see figure 13-2). In addition to the difficulties previously listed, behavioural therapists also reported that they had successfully responded to fear, coercion, depression, addiction, assault and delinquency.

p108.original: 行为治疗师专注于个体所处的环境和问题行为，而不是内在的想法、动机或感受。
p108.en: Behavioural therapists focus on the circumstances and problem behaviour of the individual, rather than on the underlying thinking, motivation or feeling.

p109.original: 就像名称所暗示的那样，行为治疗师专注于问题行为，而不是内心的想法、动机或感受。他们试图理解不良行为是如何习得的，更重要的是，如何消除不良行为并用更有效的模式代替它们。要了解如何做到这一点，我们首先来看一下从经典条件反射中借鉴的行为疗法技术。
p109.en: As the name suggests, behavioural therapists focus on problem behaviour, not on inner thoughts, motivations or feelings. They try to understand how misconduct is practiced and, more importantly, how it can be eliminated and replaced by more effective models. To understand how this can be done, we will first look at behavioural therapy techniques that are drawn from the reflection of classic conditions.

p111.original: 心理学家玛丽·科夫·琼斯（Mary Cover Jones，1924）报告说，行为疗法的首次使用是对一个叫彼得的小男孩进行治疗，他对毛茸茸的物体感到恐惧。琼斯在几周内通过逐渐让兔子在彼得吃饭时离他越来越近，从而减轻了他的恐惧。最终，彼得允许兔子站在他的腿上并抚摸它。（你可能会注意到它与约翰·华生用小艾伯特做的实验相似。的确，琼斯是华生的助手，并且了解有关小艾伯特的研究。但是，与小艾伯特不同的是，彼得接受治疗时已经对兔子和其他毛茸茸的物体产生了强烈的恐惧。）
p111.en: Psychologist Mary Cover Jones, 1924, reported that behavioural therapy was being used for the first time to treat a young boy named Peter, who was afraid of furry objects. Jones eased his fear by gradually bringing the rabbit closer to Peter for dinner in a few weeks. Eventually, Peter allowed the rabbit to stand on his leg and touch it. (You may notice it's similar to the experiment made by John Watson with little Albert. It is true that Jones was Watson's assistant and learned about little Albert's research. However, unlike little Albert, Peter had already received treatment with a strong fear of rabbits and other furry objects. I don't think so.

p112.original: 令人惊讶的是，在这次治疗后过了14年，行为疗法才重新出现，这一次是用于治疗遗尿（Mowrer & Mowrer，1938）。该方法涉及在患者身体下方放置液体敏感垫。当敏感垫因潮湿发出警报时，患者会被吵醒。这种疗法在75%的病例中是有效的，取得了惊人的成功率。因为心理动力学疗法通过谈论症状的“意义”来治疗遗尿，这根本不能解决问题。然而，行为疗法成为心理治疗的主流又花了20年的时间。
p112.en: Surprisingly, after 14 years of treatment, behavioural therapy re-emerged, this time for urine treatment (Mowrer & Mowrer, 1938). The method involves the placement of liquid sensitive mats below the patient's body. When sensitive mats are alerted by dampness, the patient is awakened. This treatment is effective in 75 per cent of cases and has achieved an alarming success rate. Because psychodynamic therapy treats urine by talking about the “means” of symptoms, it simply does not solve the problem. However, behavioural therapy has taken another 20 years to become the mainstream of psychotherapy.

p113.original: 为什么会有延迟？弗洛伊德式的古老观念（即每个症状都有潜在的无意识原因，必须予以发现和根除）在临床领域牢牢地扎下了根。这使得治疗师不敢直接干预症状（行为），因为他们担心会出现症状替代：消除一种症状后另一种可能更糟糕的症状将会取而代之。令人高兴的是，这种担心是没有根据的。
p113.en: Why is there a delay? The Freud-style old idea that every symptom has a potential unconscious cause that must be discovered and eradicated has taken firm root in the clinical field. This prevents the therapist from intervening directly with symptoms (behaviours) because they fear that there will be a substitution of symptoms: another, which may be worse, will be replaced by the elimination of one. It is gratifying that this fear is unfounded.

p114.original: 系统脱敏疗法 精神科医生约瑟夫·沃尔普（Joseph Wolpe）挑战了已经根深蒂固的症状替代概念。沃尔普认为，非理性恐惧反应和其他不良情绪行为的发展可能遵循经典条件反射模型而不是弗洛伊德模型。经典条件反射（classical conditioning）包括将新刺激与非条件刺激（unconditioned stimulus，也可称为无条件刺激）关联起来，从而使人对这两个刺激做出相同的反应。因此，恐惧反应可能与人群、蜘蛛或闪电有关。沃尔普还意识到了另一个简单的道理：
p114.en: System de-sensitization. The psychiatrist Joseph Wolpe has challenged an already entrenched concept of substitution for symptoms. According to Volpe, the development of irrational fear reactions and other unwelcome behaviour may follow the classic condition reflection model rather than the Freud model. Classical reflections include linking new and unconditioned stimulus, or unconditional stimulus, so that people react in the same way. The reaction to fear may therefore be associated with a crowd, spider or lightning. Volpe also realized another simple reason:

p115.original: 神经系统不能同时放松和活跃，因为这两个不兼容的过程不能同时被激活。将这两个想法放在一起就为沃尔普的方法（系统脱敏疗法）奠定了基础（Wolpe，1958，1973）。
p115.en: The nervous system cannot be relaxed and active at the same time, as these two incompatible processes cannot be activated at the same time. Together, these two ideas form the basis for the Volpe approach (systemic desensitization therapy) (Wolpe, 1958, 1973).

p116.original: 系统脱敏疗法（systematic desensitization）从训练程序开始，治疗师教患者放松他们的肌肉和心理（Rachman，2000）。当患者处于深度放松的状态时，治疗师会通过让患者逐渐想象更可怕的情况来达到消退（extinction）的目的。这个过程是逐步完成的，称为焦虑等级排列，治疗策略从浮想联翩到想象一个极为恐惧的情境。
p116.en: The system desensitization (systematic desensitization) starts with a training process, where the therapist teaches patients to relax their muscles and mentalities (Rachman, 2000). When the patient is in a state of deep relaxation, the therapist achieves the goal of withdrawal by allowing the patient to gradually imagine a more terrible situation. This process is gradually being completed, known as the anxiety ranking, and the treatment strategy ranges from a vision to an imagination of a situation of great fear.

p117.original: 为了建立焦虑等级，治疗师和患者首先要确定引起患者焦虑的所有情境，然后按从最弱到最强的等级进行排列（Shapiro，1995）。例如，为严重害怕公开演讲的患者构建了非条件刺激的等级排列，如表13-2所示。
p117.en: In order to establish the level of anxiety, the therapist and the patient first determine all the situations that cause the patient's anxiety, and then rank them according to the weakest to the strongest (Shapiro, 1995). For example, a hierarchy of non-conditional incentives has been established for patients who are seriously afraid to speak publicly, as shown in Table 13-2.

p119.original: 注：以上是治疗师和患者可能会构建的典型的焦虑等级，以减轻对公开演讲的恐惧感。治疗师会引导患者放松并想象以上情境。
p119.en: Note: These are typical levels of anxiety that therapists and patients may construct to reduce fear of public speaking. The therapist will guide the patient to relax and imagine the situation.

p120.original: 在脱敏过程中，已经放松下来的患者可以形象地描绘列表中最弱的焦虑刺激源。如果可以不费吹灰之力将其可视化，则患者可以继续处理下一个更强烈的焦虑刺激源。在接受几次治疗后，患者可以毫不担心地想象清单上最令人痛苦的情境（Lang & Lazovik，1963），这个过程就叫作系统脱敏。
p120.en: In the course of dissensitization, patients who have eased can visualize the weakest sources of anxiety on the list. If they can be visualized without any effort, the patient can continue to deal with the next stronger source of anxiety. After several treatments, patients can imagine without fear the most painful situation on the List (Lang & Lazovik, 1963), a process known as systematic de-sensitization.

p121.original: 事实证明，在引发患者焦虑方面，沃尔普可能过于谨慎。在一种新的和更加强烈的脱敏形式［称为暴露疗法（exposure therapy）］中，治疗师实际上可能会让患者面对其所害怕的物体或情境，如蜘蛛或蛇，而不是仅仅通过想象。与沃尔普的方法相比，这种方法似乎更有效（Barlow，2010）。该技术已成功用于众多患有恐怖症和焦虑症的患者，其中包括许多对血液、注射和细菌感到恐惧的患者，这些恐惧阻碍了他们获得所需的医学或牙科治疗（Dittmann，2005）。
p121.en: Volpe may prove too cautious in causing anxiety among patients. In a new and more intense form of dissensitisation [called exposure therapy], therapists may actually expose patients to objects or situations that they fear, such as spiders or snakes, rather than mere imagination. This approach appears to be more effective than the Volpe approach (Barlow, 2010). The technology has been successfully used for a large number of patients suffering from terror and anxiety, including many who are afraid of blood, injection and bacteria, which hinder their access to the required medical or dental treatment (Dittmann, 2005).

p122.original: 在过去的几年中，一些行为治疗师为暴露疗法增加了高科技手段。通过使用计算机生成的恐怖场景，患者可以在他们知道是安全的虚拟现实环境中探索和消除恐惧及焦虑。为了进入虚拟现实环境中，患者需要戴上一个带有屏幕的头盔，在屏幕上放映他们需要脱敏的图像的投影：蜘蛛、蛇、高处、封闭的空间，以及所有常见的导致个体产生恐怖症的物体或图像（Winerman，2005d）。
p122.en: In the past few years, some behavioural therapists have added high-tech tools to exposure therapy. Through the use of computer-generated horror scenes, patients can explore and eliminate fear and anxiety in virtual reality settings where they know they are safe. In order to enter the virtual reality environment, patients need to wear a helmet with a screen to project images on which they need to be allergic: spiders, snakes, heights, enclosed spaces, and all common objects or images that cause individual horrors (Winerman, 2005d).

p123.original: 厌恶疗法 脱敏疗法和暴露疗法可以帮助患者应对他们想要避免的刺激。但是情况相反时会如何呢？有什么方法可以帮助那些被有害或非法刺激所吸引的人呢？
p123.en: The aversion therapy, the de-sensitization therapy and the exposure therapy can help patients cope with the stimulation they want to avoid. But what happens when the opposite happens? What can be done to help those attracted by harmful or illegal incentives?

p124.original: 这些例子包括药物成瘾、某些性吸引和暴力倾向——所有这些问题都是由某些特定刺激引起的不良行为。厌恶疗法（arersion therapy）通过条件反射来解决这些问题，该条件反射旨在通过将诱因刺激物与不愉快的（厌恶的）刺激物反复配对出现以使患者感到厌恶。例如，治疗师可能会使用电击或让人产生恶心的药物，其作用是令人感到极度不愉快，但实际上对患者没有危害。随着时间的推移，对厌恶刺激的负面反应（无条件的反应）会与条件刺激（如成瘾性药物）相关联，让患者产生厌恶情绪，进而取代之前的欲望。
p124.en: These include drug addiction, certain sexual attractions and violent tendencies — all of which are caused by certain specific incentives. The problem is addressed by the retrogression of conditions designed to make patients sick by setting up repeated pairs of irritation with unpleasant (aversion) irritation. For example, the potential use of electroshocks by therapists or the generation of disgusting drugs has the effect of being extremely unpleasant, but in practice is not harmful to patients. Over time, negative reactions to aversion (unconditional responses) are associated with conditions of stimulation (e.g. addiction drugs), which creates an aversion for the patient and replaces previous desires.

p125.original: 再例如，如果你选择使用厌恶疗法戒烟，则可能需要在你吸烟时制造出难闻的气味，—直到你在吸烟与恶心之间建立牢固的联系为止，如图13-3所示。让酗酒者在喝酒时服用安塔布司（促进清醒的药物）也有类似的条件反应。
p125.en: And, for example, if you choose to quit smoking with aversion therapy, it may be necessary to create a bad smell when you smoke -- until you establish a strong link between smoking and nausea, as shown in figure 13-3. Similar conditions are observed for alcohol users to take Andabus (sensitization drugs) while drinking.

p126.original: 图13-3 对吸烟厌恶的条件反射
p126.en: Figure 13-3 Conditional reflection of tobacco aversion

p127.original: 注：针对吸烟的厌恶疗法可能会在个体吸烟时制造恶臭的气味。恶臭（如腐烂的鸡蛋）会让人感到恶心。然后，该反应成为与吸烟相关的条件反应。
p127.en: Note: The aversion therapy for smoking may create a odour in individual smoking. It stinks (e.g. rotten eggs) and it makes people sick. The response then becomes a conditional response associated with smoking.

p128.original: 从某种角度来看，厌恶疗法与酷刑无异。那么，为什么有人会情愿接受这种疗法呢？有时，法院可能会判定缓刑犯接受这种治疗。但是，通常人们接受这种类型治疗的原因是他们的成瘾性很强，抵制了其他治疗方法。
p128.en: From a certain point of view, aversion to therapy is no different from torture. So, why would anyone be willing to take this treatment? In some cases, the court may sentence a suspended offender to such treatment. However, this type of treatment is usually provided because they are highly addictive and resist other treatments.

p130.original: 四岁的泰勒（Tyler）和父母一起去商店会大声尖叫，因为父母拒绝给他买糖果。当父母屈服于他的要求时，他通过操作性条件反射习得了这种令人讨厌的行为。实际上，在儿童和成年人中发现的大多数行为问题都是通过奖励和惩罚形成的。例如，泰勒的案例与长期上班迟到的员工或等到最后一刻才复习准备考试的学生之间有相似之处。改变这种行为需要操作性条件反射技术。
p130.en: Four-year-old Tyler and his parents would scream at the store because they refused to buy him candy. When the parents surrendered to his demands, he was exposed to such abhorrent behaviour through operational reflexes. In fact, most behavioural problems found among children and adults are the result of rewards and punishment. For example, there is a similarity between the Taylor case and long-term late staff or students who wait until the last minute to review their preparation for the examination. Changing such behaviour requires operational conditions reflective technology.

p131.original: 让我们看一下关于操作性条件反射的两种治疗方法。
p131.en: Let's look at two treatments for operational reflexes.

p132.original: 相倚性管理 泰勒的父母可以通过转移自己的注意力（即不关注泰勒的尖叫）来学着在商店里消除他的尖叫反应，当然这绝非易事。此外，治疗师可能会指导他们“关注泰勒的良好表现”，并给予他所有需要的关注，但仅限于良好的表现。随着时间的推移，不断强化的变化将取代旧的不良行为，并有助于使新的行为得以维持。这种方法是相倚性管理（contingency management）的示例：通过调节行为的结果来改变行为本身。它已被证明可以有效地治疗在家庭、学校、工作、监狱、军队和精神病院等各种环境中出现的问题行为。谨慎地运用奖惩措施还可以减少孤独症儿童的自残行为（Frith，1997）。而且，如果你想改变一些不良习惯或养成新习惯，甚至可以对自己应用相倚性管理技术，请参阅下面的“试一试”。
p132.en: It's not easy, of course, for Taylor's parents to learn to eliminate his screams in the store by diverting their attention (i.e. not paying attention to Taylor's screams). In addition, the therapists may guide them to “pay attention to Taylor's good performance” and give him all the attention he needs, but only to good performance. Over time, incremental changes will replace old malpractices and help sustain new behaviours. This approach is an example of interdependencies management: changing the conduct itself by regulating the outcome of the act. It has proved to be effective in treating problematic behaviour in various settings, including the home, school, work, prison, army and psychiatric hospitals. The prudent application of incentives and penalties can also reduce self-harm among autistic children (Frith, 1997). Moreover, if you want to change some bad habits or develop new ones, you can even apply the technology of mutual trust management to yourself, see the following “tries”.

p133.original: 试一试 行为自我矫正

p134.original: 你想养成一种习惯吗？让我们考虑一下如何养成规律运动的习惯，以行为自我矫正程序为例，你可以适应该行为以获取任何新的理想行为模式或摆脱不良行为。在回答以下问题时，请从行为的角度指出哪些答案是合适的。
p134.en: Do you want to grow a habit? Let us consider how the habit of a regular movement can be developed, for example, by means of behavioural self-correction procedures, which you can adapt to acquire any new ideal pattern of behaviour or escape from bad behaviour. In answering the following questions, please indicate which answers are appropriate from the point of view of behaviour.

p135.original: 以下哪种行为是开发和维护新的锻炼计划的理想行为？
p135.en: Which of the following are the ideal behaviours for developing and maintaining new exercise programmes?

p170.original: 代币制 有一种特殊的治疗方法被称为代币制（token economy），可用于教室和学校等团体环境。我们可以将其视为团体治疗的行为版本（Ayllon & Azrin，1968；Martin & Pear，1999）。该方法的名称来自治疗师或教师有时会为表扬他们所期望的行为而提供直接强化的塑料代币。
p170.en: There is a special treatment known as token economy, which can be used in community settings such as classrooms and schools. We can see it as a group-treated version of behaviour (Ayllon & Azrin, 1968; Martin & Pear, 1999. The name of the method comes from plastic coins that are sometimes provided by therapists or teachers to provide direct reinforcements in recognition of their desired behaviour.

p171.original: 例如，在课堂上，学生可能会因安静地坐几分钟、参与课堂讨论或按时交作业而获得代币。随后，学生可以用代币兑换食物、商品或特权。通常，治疗师也会使用“点数”或游戏币来代替代币。重要的是，个体在做出一些期许的反应后要立即给他们一些强化物。通过适当的调整，代币制还可以很好地用于发育障碍儿童、精神病患者以及监狱里的犯人（Higgins et al.，2001）。
p171.en: For example, in the classroom, students may receive tokens for sitting quietly for a few minutes, participating in class discussions or working on time. The student may then exchange a token currency for food, goods or privileges. Often, therapists also use “points” or game coins to replace coins. It is important that individuals are given some reinforcements immediately after they have made some of the promised responses. With appropriate adjustments, the currency system can also be used well for children with developmental difficulties, mentally ill persons and prisoners in prisons (Higgins et al., 2001).

p175.original: 13.4.3 参与性模仿：观察学习疗法

p176.original: 我们经常说“东施效颦”。果然，猴子可以通过观察和模仿学习恐惧。一项研究表明，以前对蛇不反感的实验室猴子可以通过观察它们的父母对真正的蛇和玩具蛇的恐惧反应而获得恐蛇症。猴子看到蛇时越不安，它们的后代见到蛇时就越害怕（Mineka et al.，1984）。一项后续研究表明，这种恐惧不仅仅是家庭问题。当其他以前没有表现出对蛇感到恐惧的猴子有机会观察与其无血缘关系的成年猴子做出对蛇感到害怕反应时，它们很快就学会了相同的反应，如图13-4所示（Cook et al，1985）。
p176.en: We often say, "Tung Fu." And indeed, monkeys can learn fear by observing and imitating. A study has shown that laboratory monkeys who were previously unsatisfied with snakes can obtain snake disease by observing their parents ' fear of real snakes and toy snakes. The more unsettling the monkeys look at the snake, the more afraid their offspring are when they see the snake (Mineka et al., 1984). A follow-up study has shown that such fear is not just a family issue. When other monkeys who had not previously shown fear of snakes had the opportunity to observe the reaction of adults who were not related to them, they quickly learned the same reaction, as shown in figure 13-4 (Cook et al., 1985).

p177.original: 图13-4 猴子的害怕反应

p178.original: 人们也会像猴子一样通过观察他人的行为习得恐惧。但出于治疗的目的，参与性模仿的观察学习也可以被用于健康行为的养成。在参与性模仿（participant modeling）中，来访者或参与者观察并模仿某人的期望行为。当然，多年来体育教练一直使用参与性模仿。与之类似，治疗恐蛇症的行为治疗师可能会通过首先接近笼中的蛇，然后做出触摸蛇等模拟期望的行为。然后，来访者模仿想要学习的示范行为——但绝不是被迫学习。如果治疗师感觉到来访者的抗拒，来访者可能会回到之前的水平。如你所见，该过程类似于系统脱敏，但重要的是增加了观察学习。事实上，参与性模仿借鉴了操作性条件反射和经典条件反射的概念。
p178.en: People learn fear by watching other people's behavior, like monkeys. However, for therapeutic purposes, participatory imitation of observational learning can also be used for healthy behaviour formation. In participatory mimics, visitors or participants observe and imitate a person's expected behaviour. Of course, for many years, sports coaches have been using participatory imitations. Similarly, behaviour therapists who treat snake disease may engage in simulated desired behaviour by approaching snakes first in cages and then by touching snakes. Then, visitors imitate the model behaviour that they want to learn — but in no way are they forced to learn. If the therapist feels resistance from the visitors, they may return to their previous levels. As you can see, the process is similar to system dissensitization, but it is important to increase observational learning. In fact, participatory imitations draw on the concepts of operational and classical conditions.

p179.original: 在一项与其他几种方法进行比较的研究中，可以看出参与性模仿在消除蛇恐症方面的巨大作用：
p179.en: In a study comparing several other methods, it can be seen that participatory imitation plays a significant role in the eradication of snake fear:

p180.en: 1. Symbolic imitation, a technique that indirectly exposes objects by watching films or videos, and simulates the handling of frightening situations;

p181.original: 2. 脱敏疗法，你也许记得，也就是将被试暴露于想象中的可怕刺激中；
p181.en: 2. De-sensitization therapy, which you may recall will be exposed to the ghastly irritation that was imagined;

p183.original: 如图13-5所示，参与性模仿最为成功。参与性模仿组12名被试中有11名消除了恐蛇症（Bandura，1970）。
p183.en: Participatory imitations are the most successful, as shown in figures 13-5. Eleven of the 12 participants in the participatory imitation group were tested to eliminate snake disease (Bandura, 1970).

p184.original: 图13-5 不同疗法消除恐蛇症的效果对比
p184.en: Figure 13-5 Comparison of the effects of different treatments in combating snake disease
