p185.en: Note: Visitors are able to approach snakes after watching imitations. The map compares participatory imitation therapy with two other therapies and a control group.

p188.original: 解释认知行为疗法与领悟疗法和行为疗法的不同。
p188.en: Explain the difference between cognitive behaviour therapy and cognitive and behavioural therapy.

p189.original: 假设每次你所爱的人对他人表示友好时，你都难以控制嫉妒的情绪。问题很可能源于你对自己和其他相关人员的认知（“马蒂正在从我身边偷走特里”）。这些想法也可能会影响你的行为，这些行为方式可能会使特里远离你。在这种情况下，针对你的认知和行为一起进行治疗可能比单独治疗更好。
p189.en: Assuming that every time someone you love is friendly to others, you have difficulty controlling jealousy. The problem is probably due to your perception of yourself and other persons involved (“Marty is stealing Terry from me”). These ideas may also affect your behaviour, which may keep Terry away from you. In such cases, it may be better to treat your cognitive and behavioural behaviour together than to treat it alone.

p190.original: 简而言之，认知行为疗法（cognitive-behavioral therapy，CBT）把对思想和态度的认知重点与我们刚刚讨论的行为策略结合起来。这种双重方法假设，不合理的自我陈述通常是适应不良行为的基础。因此，需要治疗师和来访者共同努力来修正非理性的自我对话，设定可以实现的行为目标，制定实现这些目标的现实策略，并评估结果。通过这种方式，人们可以改变处理问题的方式，逐渐发展出新技能和自我效能感（Bandura，1986，1992；DeAngelis，2008b；Schwarzer，1992）。
p190.en: In short, cognitive behavior therapy (cognitive-behavioral therapy, CBT) combines the cognitive focus on ideas and attitudes with the behavioural strategies we have just discussed. This dual approach assumes that unreasonable self-representation is usually the basis for adaptation to bad behaviour. It is therefore necessary to work together with therapists and visitors to correct irrational self-dialogues, set achievable behavioural goals, develop realistic strategies to achieve them and assess results. In this way, people can change the way they deal with the problem and develop new skills and self-effectiveness (Bandura, 1986, 1992); DeAngelis, 2008b; Schwarzer, 1992.

p191.original: 认知行为疗法的效果如何？你怎么看？
p191.en: What are the effects of cognitive behavioral therapy? What do you think?

p192.original: 效果确实很好，特别是对于抑郁症、焦虑症、酗酒、神经性贪食症、反复出现的噩梦和创伤后应激障碍（Baker et al.，2008；Chamberlin，2008）。事实上，它是心理学中最成功的疗法。在所有这些障碍中，CBT至少可以和药物治疗一样有效——有时甚至更有效。对于某些其他情况，如双相障碍和精神分裂症，CBT和药物的组合比单独使用其中一种都更有效。
p192.en: It does work well, especially for depression, anxiety, alcohol abuse, neurological hunger, recurring nightmares and post-traumatic stress disorder (Baker et al., 2008); Chamberlin, 2008. In fact, it is the most successful therapy in psychology. Of all these obstacles, CBT can be at least as effective — and sometimes even more effective — as medication. For some other cases, such as dual disorder and schizophrenia, the combination of CBT and drugs is more effective than the single use of one of them.

p194.original: 最著名的认知行为疗法是由阿尔伯特·艾利斯（Albert Ellis，1987，1990，1996）创造的，旨在帮助人们消除自我挫败的思维模式。艾利斯将他的治疗方法称为理性情绪行为疗法（rational-emotive behavior therapy，REBT），这个名字来源于它挑战了某些“非理性”信念和行为。
p194.en: The most famous cognitive behaviour therapy was created by Albert Ellis, 1987, 1990, 1996, to help people eliminate self-defeating thinking patterns. Ellis called his treatment rational-emotive emotional behavior therapy (Rictional-emotive therapy, REBT), a name derived from which he challenged certain “unrational” beliefs and behaviours.

p195.original: REBT挑战了哪些非理性信念？它们如何导致了适应不良的感觉和行为？根据艾利斯的说法，适应不良的人将生活建立在一系列不切实际的价值观和无法实现的目标上。这些无法实现的目标和不切实际的价值观导致人们抱有不现实的期望，即他们应该永远成功，他们应该永远得到认可，他们应该永远被公平对待，他们的经历应该永远是愉快的。你可以在下面的“试一试”版块中看到最常见的非理性信念。例如，在你自己的日常生活中，你可能经常告诉自己你的数学考试成绩“应该”是A或者你“应该”每天花1小时锻炼身体。此外，他说，如果你无法实现自己的目标并且很少质疑这种“神经质”的自说自话，它可能会控制你的行为，甚至阻止你选择自己想要的生活。如果你准备接受REBT的治疗，你的治疗师会教你如何识别这些假设，质疑它们的合理性，并用更有效的想法替换非理性的想法。艾利斯告诫大家，不要总对自己说“应该”。
p195.en: What irrational beliefs does REBT challenge? How have they led to poorly adapted feelings and behaviours? According to Ellis, people who are not well-adapted base their lives on a set of unrealistic values and unattainable goals. These unattainable goals and unrealistic values lead to unrealistic expectations that they should always succeed, that they should always be recognized, that they should always be treated fairly and that their experiences should always be happy. You can see the most common irrational beliefs in the "Try" section below. For example, in your own daily life, you may often tell yourself that your math test grades are "should" A or "should" take an hour of physical exercise every day. Moreover, he said that if you failed to achieve your goals and rarely questioned the “nervous” self-proclaimer, it might control your behaviour and even prevent you from choosing the life you wanted. If you're ready for REBT treatment, your therapist will teach you how to recognize these assumptions, question their legitimacy and replace irrational ideas with more effective ideas. Alex warned you not to say “should”.

p196.original: 试一试 检查你自己的信念

p197.original: 下列是一些明显非理性的信念，但阿尔伯特·艾利斯发现许多人都具有这些信念。你有这些想法吗？自省内心并坦诚地回答：以下哪些最符合你的真实感受。
p197.en: The following are clearly irrational beliefs, but Albert Ellis found many of them. Do you have any ideas? The answer is self-critical and honest: which of the following is the most appropriate for your true feelings.

p198.original: 1. 我必须得到大家的喜爱和认可。
p198.en: 1. I must be loved and recognized by all.

p199.original: 2. 我必须完全胜任各种工作、有能力并且有成就。
p199.en: I must be fully competent, competent and successful.

p200.original: 3. 当事情没有按照我想要的方式发展时，这就是灾难性的。
p200.en: 3. It is catastrophic when things do not go the way I want.

p201.original: 4. 感到不快乐源于我无法控制一些事情。
p201.en: 4. The sense of unhappiness stems from something I cannot control.

p202.original: 5. 人们必须始终公平公正地对待彼此，那些不这样做的人是讨厌和可怕的人。
p202.en: 5. People must always treat each other fairly and justly, and those who do not do so are annoying and terrible.

p203.original: 6. 我必须时刻警惕危险和可能出错的事情。
p203.en: 6. I must remain vigilant about dangers and possible mistakes.

p204.original: 7. 生活充满问题，我要快速地找到解决它们的办法。
p204.en: Life is full of problems, and I want to find solutions to them quickly.

p205.original: 8. 与面对问题和责任相比，逃避它们更容易。
p205.en: It is easier to avoid them than to face problems and responsibilities.

p206.original: 9. 过去不愉快的经历对我产生了深远的影响，因此，它们一定会继续影响我现在的感受和行动。
p206.en: 9. The past unpleasant experiences have had a profound impact on me, and they will certainly continue to affect my feelings and actions now.

p207.original: 10. 我只享受当前的快乐。未来的问题自会迎刃而解。
p207.en: 10. I am only enjoying the present pleasure. The problems of the future will be solved.

p208.original: 在艾利斯看来，所有这些陈述都源于非理性的信念，都可能会导致心理问题。你符合的条目越多，你的信念就越“不合理”。他的认知行为疗法被称为理性情绪行为疗法，专注于帮助人们认识到，这些非理性的信念会“把自己逼疯”。例如，一个去参加聚会而不是为考试而学习的学生持有上述信念的第8条。一个因得不到某份工作而感到沮丧的人持有上述信念的第3条。你可以从艾利斯的书中获得更多关于这个疗法的信息。
p208.en: In the view of Ellis, all these statements were based on irrational beliefs and could lead to psychological problems. The more entries you meet, the more your faith is “unjustified”. His cognitive behaviour therapy, known as rational emotional behaviour therapy, is focused on helping people realize that these irrational beliefs “puzzled themselves mad”. For example, article 8 of the above-mentioned beliefs is held by a student who goes to a party and does not study for the examination. Article 3 of the above-mentioned beliefs is held by a person who is frustrated by the lack of a job. You can get more information about this therapy from Ellis's book.

p209.original: 那么，你认为认知行为治疗师会如何处理弗洛伊德的强迫症患者？
p209.en: So, what do you think the cognitive therapist would do with Freud's compulsive patients?

p210.original: 正如我们之前所建议的，治疗师会首先采用认知方法挑战女孩的非理性信念。然后，切换到行为模式，治疗师可能会教女孩每天晚上入睡前使用放松技巧。这些技巧将取代强迫性的仪式。治疗师也可能会与女孩的父母一起协作，专注于帮助他们学会不去关注女孩的仪式化行为，因为这种关注对女孩无异于是一种奖励。
p210.en: As we have suggested before, therapists will first challenge the irrational beliefs of girls using cognitive methods. The behaviour pattern is then changed, and the therapist may teach the girl to use relaxing techniques every night before she goes to bed. These techniques will replace forced rituals. The therapists may also work with the girls ' parents to focus on helping them learn not to focus on girls ' ritualization, as such attention is a reward for girls.

p211.original: 同样，针对德里克，认知行为治疗师会通过挑战他的思维方式来提供帮助——也许是少责怪自己，更多地关注做得更好的建设性计划——最终可以改变他的感受和行为方式。事实上，彼得·卢因森（Peter Lewinsohn）和他的同事们发现，他们可以用这种认知行为技术有效地治疗很多抑郁症患者（Lewinsohn et al.，1980，1990；Lewinsohn & Gottlib，1995）。他们的方法是，在抑郁循环的几个点上进行干预，教人们如何改变他们的无助感，如何适应不愉快的情境，并在他们的生活中构建更多的奖赏。
p211.en: Similarly, for Derek, cognitive behaviour therapists will help by challenging his way of thinking — perhaps less blaming themselves and more focusing on more constructive plans to do better — and ultimately change his feelings and behaviour. In fact, Peter Lewinsohn and his colleagues found that they could use this cognitive behavior technique to effectively treat many people suffering from depression (Lewinsohn et al., 1980, 1990); Lewinsohn & Gottlib, 1995. Their approach is to intervene at several points in the cycle of depression, to teach people how to change their feelings of helplessness, how to adapt to an unpleasant situation and build more rewards in their lives.

p213.original: 德里克也可能是一种认知行为治疗新范式的理想患者人选，这种新方法被称为积极心理疗法（positive psychotherapy，PPT），由马丁·塞利格曼（Martin Seligman）开创。与人本主义者一样，塞利格曼和他的积极心理学同行们将他们的使命视为在心理学对精神障碍负面的强调与他们对成长、健康和幸福的积极关注之间找到平衡。因此，塞利格曼通过强调积极因素来解决抑郁症问题是“自然而然的”（seligman et al.，2006）。然而，不同于人本主义者，PPT侧重于认知和行为，并重视研究。
p213.en: Derek may also be an ideal patient for a new paradigm of cognitive behaviour therapy, known as active psychotherapy (PPT), initiated by Martin Seligman. Like humanists, Séligman and his active psychological colleagues see their mission as balancing the negative emphasis on mental disorders with their positive interest in growth, health and well-being. Therefore, Seligman addressed depression “naturally” by emphasizing positive factors (Seligman et al., 2006). However, unlike humanists, PPT focuses on cognitive and behavioural aspects and on research.

p214.original: 在PPT和卢因森的治疗中，德里克可能会发现自己更像一个学生而非病人。例如，治疗师可能会给他布置一个“家庭作业”，如睡觉前写下今天进展顺利的三件事及为什么进展顺利。德里克还将学会关注积极情绪，建设性地回应他人，以及在工作和家庭生活中寻求更多乐趣。PPT的效果如何？塞利格曼和他的团队已经对几十名来访者使用了积极心理疗法，并报告了初步结果且显示它比传统疗法或抗抑郁药物能够更有效地缓解抑郁症（Seligman et al.，2006）。
p214.en: In PPT and Luinson's treatment, Derek may find himself more like a student than a patient. For example, the therapist may have assigned him a “homework”, such as writing three things that are going well today before sleeping and why they are going well. Derek will also learn to be active, to respond constructively to others and to seek more pleasure in working and family life. How's the PPT working out? Séligman and his team have already used active psychotherapy for dozens of visitors and reported on preliminary results and showed that it is more effective in alleviating depression than traditional therapy or antidepressants (Seligman et al., 2006).

p215.original: 13.5.3 通过改变思想来改变大脑
p215.en: 13.5.3 Changing the Brain by Changing Minds

p216.original: 当前的脑部扫描技术表明，认知行为疗法不仅可以帮助人们改变思想，还可以改变大脑（Dobbs，2006b）。在一项研究中，治疗师对强迫症患者（如经常担心自己没有关火或锁门）进行了认知行为矫正（Schwartz et al.，1996）。当他们有想跑回家检查的冲动时，治疗师就让他们接受训练，并将自己的经历标记为强迫症或冲动，而不是理性的担忧。接下来的15分钟让他们专注于其他活动以分散自己的注意力并等待这种“冲动”消失，而不是屈服于它，通过对接受了这种技术训练的被试的大脑进行的PET扫描表明，随着时间的推移，大脑中负责那些恼人的恐惧或冲动的区域逐渐变得不那么活跃了。
p216.en: Current brain scanning techniques show that cognitive behaviour therapy can help people not only to change their mind, but also their brain (Dobbs, 2006b). In one study, the therapists had a cognitive behavioural correction for patients with coercive diseases (e.g., often fearing that they were not involved in fire or locking the door) (Schwartz et al., 1996). When they have the urge to run home for testing, the therapists train them and mark their experience as an imposition or an impulse rather than a rational fear. The next 15 minutes have allowed them to focus on other activities to distract themselves and wait for the “moment” to disappear, rather than yield to it, as evidenced by the PET scan of the tested brain that has been trained in this technology, which has become less active over time in the brain, responsible for the fear or impulses of the people.

p217.original: 正如该研究表明的那样，自从我们怀疑思想和行为是先天还是后天的产物以来，心理学已经取得了长足的进步。通过认知行为疗法，我们现在知道经历是可以改变行为背后的生物学过程的。
p217.en: As the study shows, since we doubted whether ideas and behaviours were the product of birth or of birth, psychology has made great strides. Through cognitive behavioral therapy, we now know that the biological processes behind behaviour can be changed.

p220.original: 解释艾森克对治疗的批评，并描述治疗有效的证据。
p220.en: Explain Eisenke's criticism of the treatment and describe evidence of its effectiveness.

p221.original: 既然我们已经了解了各种类型的心理疗法（见图13-6），让我们退后一步，看一看心理疗法的效果如何。
p221.en: Now that we have learned about the various types of psychotherapy (see figures 13-6), let us take a step back and see how well psychotherapy works.

p222.original: 想一想：如何客观地判断心理疗法是否真的有效？正如我们将看到的，这个问题的答案始终不那么明确（Kopta et al.，1999；Shadish et al.，2000）。
p222.en: Think about it: How to objectively judge whether psychotherapy is really effective? As we will see, the answer to this question has always been less clear (Kopta et al., 1999); Shadish et al., 2000.

p223.original: 大量证据表明，大多数接受过心理治疗的人都喜欢心理治疗。例如，通过对《消费者报告》（Consumer Reports，1995）的数千名订阅者进行的调查就表明了这一点。受访者需指出他们感受心理治疗帮助自己的程度，他们对治疗师的治疗满意度如何，治疗结束后他们的“整体情绪状态”有多大变化，以及他们具体接受了什么样的治疗。调查结果如下：
p223.en: There is ample evidence that the majority of those who have undergone psychological treatment prefer it. This was demonstrated, for example, by a survey of thousands of subscribers to the Consumer Reports 1995. Interviewees need to indicate the extent to which they feel that psychological care helps them, how well they are satisfied with the treatment of the therapist, how much their “comprehensive emotional state” has changed after the treatment has ended, and what treatment they have actually received. The findings are as follows:

p224.original: （1）治疗是有效的，也就是说，心理治疗被认为可以帮助来访者减少或消除他们的心理问题；
p224.en: (1) Treatment is effective, i.e. psychological treatment is considered to help visitors reduce or eliminate their psychological problems;

p225.en: (2) Long-term treatment is better than short-term treatment;

p226.original: （3）所有形式的治疗对于改善来访者的问题都同样有效（Jacobson & Christensen，1996）。
p226.en: (3) All forms of treatment are equally effective in improving the problems of visitors (Jacobson & Christensen, 1996).

p227.original: 然而，我们不能仅仅因为人们说他们喜欢心理治疗或心理治疗对他们有帮助而对心理治疗竖起大拇指（Hollon，1996）。感性认识不能成为科学的证据——这就是为什么心理学家现在要求通过有对照组或控制组的研究来判断治疗效果。因此，让我们转向对治疗有效性的对照研究，从一份几乎颠覆治疗方案的报告开始。
p227.en: However, we cannot stick our thumbs to therapy simply because people say they like therapy or that it helps them (Hollon, 1996). Sensual awareness cannot be a scientific evidence - that is why psychologists now require that the effects of treatment be judged by research with a control or control group. Let us therefore turn to a comparative study of the effectiveness of treatment, beginning with a report of an almost subversive treatment programme.

p228.original: 图13-6 不同类型疗法的比较
p228.en: Figure 13-6 Comparison of different types of therapy

p230.original: 关于治疗有效性的讨论在1952年达到了一个顶峰，当时英国心理学家汉斯·艾森克（Hans Eysenck）宣称，大约有三分之二的非精神病性患者会在两年内康复，无论他们是否接受过治疗。艾森克的证据来自对各种领悟疗法的几项研究结果的回顾，所有这些研究都将接受治疗的患者与那些在等待治疗的患者进行了比较。他指出，等待治疗名单上的康复者与接受治疗康复者一样多。从表面上看，这意味着心理治疗基本上一文不值——和完全不治疗一个样！至少治疗师对这个结果并不满意。但艾森克的挑战产生了巨大的效应：它激发了治疗师开始对他们所使用疗法的有效性展开了大量的研究。
p230.en: The discussion on the effectiveness of treatment reached a peak in 1952, when the British psychologist Hans Eysenck claimed that about two thirds of non-psychiatric patients would recover within two years, whether or not they had received treatment. Eisenke's evidence is a review of several studies of various epithetological treatments, all of which compare patients receiving treatment with those waiting for treatment. He notes that the waiting list for treatment is as large as the waiting list for treatment. On the face of it, that means that therapy is basically worthless — and completely untreated! At least the therapist is not satisfied with this result. But the challenge of Eisenke has had a tremendous effect: it has inspired therapists to begin a great deal of research into the effectiveness of the therapy they use.

p231.original: 对艾森克的回应 1970年（Meltzoff & Kornreich）、1975年（Luborsky et al.）和1977年（Smith & Glass）开始出现关于治疗效果证据的文献综述。总体而言，这些文献（约有375项研究）支持两个主要结论。
p231.en: A synthesis of the literature on evidence of therapeutic effects began to appear in 1970 (Meltzoff & Kornreich), 1975 (Luborsky et al.) and 1977 (Smith & Glass). In general, these literatures (approximately 375 studies) support two main conclusions.

p232.original: 首先，艾森克显然高估了无治疗对照组的改善率。
p232.en: First of all, Eisenke clearly overestimated the improvement rate of the no-treatment control group.

p233.original: 其次，治疗比不治疗更有效——这让每个人都松了一口气！
p233.en: Second, treatment is more effective than non-treatment — it's a relief for everyone!

p234.original: 然后，逐渐出现了支持心理治疗具有价值的科学共识（Meredith，1986；VandenBos，1986）。事实上，对于范围广泛的障碍，心理治疗已被证明具有与许多已进行的医疗实践相当或更好的效果（Wampold，2007）。此外，研究开始表明，治疗不仅在西方工业化国家（美国、加拿大和欧洲各国）有效，而且在世界各地的各种文化环境中也有效（Beutler & Machado，1992；Lipsey & Wilson，1993）。
p234.en: A scientific consensus of value for supporting psychotherapy then emerged (Meredith, 1986); VandenBos, 1986. In fact, for a wide range of barriers, psychotherapy has proved to have a comparable or better effect than many medical practices that have been undertaken (Wampold, 2007). In addition, research has begun to show that treatment is effective not only in industrialized Western countries (the United States, Canada and European countries), but also in various cultural settings around the world (Beutler & Machado, 1992); Lipsey & Wilson, 1993.

p235.original: 新的问题 但新研究引发了新的问题。
p235.en: New issues, but new research has given rise to new problems.

p236.original: 某些疗法是否比其他疗法更好？
p236.en: Are some treatments better than others?

p237.original: 我们能否确定某些具体障碍最适合的疗法？
p237.en: Can we identify the most appropriate treatments for some of the specific barriers?

p238.original: 史密斯和格拉斯（Smith & Glass，1977）的调查显示这些问题的答案都是“是”。史密斯和格拉斯发现，对于许多焦虑症的治疗，行为疗法似乎比领悟疗法更具优势。正如我们之前所指出的，使用认知行为疗法治疗抑郁症、焦虑症、神经性贪食症和其他几种障碍现在得到了可靠的实践支持。此外，最近的评估显示，领悟疗法也可以有效地用于治疗诸如夫妻关系不协调、抑郁甚至难以治疗的人格障碍等问题（Shedler，2010）。事实上，现在有一个明显的趋势是将特定疗法与特定条件相匹配。
p238.en: The Smith & Glass survey, 1977, shows that the answers to these questions are “Yes”. Smith and Glass found that behavioural therapy seemed to be more advantageous than epithetic therapy for many anxiety disorders. As we have pointed out before, the use of cognitive behaviour therapy for the treatment of depression, anxiety, neuro-eating and several other disorders is now supported by reliable practice. In addition, recent assessments have shown that episodic therapy can be used effectively to treat issues such as uncoordinated, depressed and even difficult personality disorders (Shedler, 2010). In fact, there is a clear trend towards matching specific treatments with specific conditions.

p239.original: 最后，我们应该注意到，在评估各种心理疗法的效果时，重要的是要认识到治疗成功并非意味着“治愈”。有时，仅做出改善就是我们所能期望的全部成功。例如，在治疗精神分裂症、智力障碍或孤独症时，当患有这些疾病的人学习更多适应性行为并报告过上了更幸福的生活时，心理疗法就被认为是有效的（Hogarty et al.，1997）。
p239.en: Finally, we should note that, in assessing the effectiveness of the various psychotherapy programmes, it is important to recognize that success does not mean “cure”. Sometimes improvements alone are the full success that we can expect. For example, when treating schizophrenia, mental disorders or autism, psychotherapy is considered effective when people with these diseases learn more to adapt to sexual behaviour and report on a happier life (Hogarty et al., 1997).

p240.original: 心理学很有用 大多数人从哪里获得帮助
p240.en: Psychology works. Where does most people get help?

p241.original: 心理治疗对各种心理问题的有效性似乎毋庸置疑。话虽如此，但我们应该再次承认，大多数经历精神困扰的人不会向专业治疗师寻求帮助。相反，他们求助于社区中的“非专业人士”（Wills & DePaulo，1991）。那些有精神问题的人通常会求助于朋友、牧师、美发师、调酒师和其他他们信任的人。事实上，对于某些类型的问题——也许是日常生活中最常见的问题——一个有同情心的朋友可能和训练有素的专业治疗师达到同样的效果（Berman & Norton，1985；Christensen & Jacobson，1994）。
p241.en: The effectiveness of psychotherapy for various psychological problems seems unquestionable. That being said, we should acknowledge once again that most people who experience mental distress do not seek help from professional therapists. Instead, they turn to “unprofessionals” in the community (Wills & DePaulo, 1991). Those with mental problems usually turn to friends, priests, hairdressers, barbers and others they trust. Indeed, for certain types of problems — perhaps most common in everyday life — a sympathetic friend may have the same effect as a trained professional therapist (Berman & Norton, 1985); Christensen & Jacobson, 1994.

p243.original: 大多数精神问题并不是在DSM-5中占据中心位置的严重障碍。相反，大多数人面临的心理困扰是由于失业、婚姻困扰、孩子行为不端、友谊破裂、心爱之人去世……简言之，最常见的问题包括混乱、困惑、选择、挫折、压力及丧失。发现自己处于这些适应困难的人可能不需要心理治疗、药物治疗或其他一些特殊治疗。他们需要有人来帮助他们厘清问题。通常这意味着他们会求助于像你这样的普通人。
p243.en: Most mental problems are not a serious obstacle to a central position in DSM-5. On the contrary, the psychological distress faced by the majority of the population is due to unemployment, marital distress, child misconduct, broken friendships and the death of loved ones... In short, the most common problems include confusion, confusion, choice, frustration, stress and loss. Persons who find themselves in such difficult situations of adaptation may not need psychological, pharmaceutical or other special treatment. They need someone to help them clear up their problems. Usually it means they turn to ordinary people like you.

p244.original: 那么，如果有人向你求助，你会怎么做？
p244.en: So, what would you do if someone asked for your help?

p245.original: 1. 你应该记住，有些问题确实需要专业人士来解决，如自杀威胁或意图伤害他人的迹象。你应该为有这种倾向的人寻求有能力的专业人士的帮助。
p245.en: 1. You should remember that there are problems that do require professional solutions, such as threats of suicide or signs of intent to harm others. You should seek the help of competent professionals for people with such tendencies.

p246.original: 2. 你应该记住，大多数治疗方法都需要经过特殊培训，尤其是那些需要认知行为治疗技术或心理动力学解释的方法。
p246.en: 2. It should be borne in mind that most treatments require special training, especially those that require cognitive behaviour therapy techniques or psychokinetic interpretation.

p247.original: 我们敦促你尽可能多地了解这些方法——但我们强烈建议你将操作留给专业人士。然而，其他一些技巧只是良好人际关系的延伸，它们完全属于普通人能够进行心理“急救”的能力范围。
p247.en: We urge you to be as aware of these methods as possible — but we strongly recommend that you leave the operation to the professionals. Other techniques, however, are simply extensions of good interpersonal relationships and are well within the reach of the ability of ordinary people to perform psychological “first aid”.

p248.original: 简言之，我们将考虑其中三个：
p248.en: In short, we will consider three of them:

p249.original: 倾听：如果你只是倾听，那么很少会出错。有时，被倾听是处于困境中的人所需要的全部治疗。它的工作原理是鼓励个体将问题组织得足够好以进行交流。因此，那些直言不讳的人往往会自己得出解决方案。作为一个积极的倾听者（active listener），你可以通过向对方提供反馈来进一步发挥作用：点头、保持一种表现出感兴趣的表情、复述对方的话，并在你不明白时询问。正如我们在前面的以来访者为中心的疗法相关内容中所看到的，积极倾听让对方知道听者是有兴趣的和有同理心的（与他人的感受一致）。同时，如果你能避免提建议，你会表现得更好，因为这些建议会剥夺说话者自己得出解决方案的机会。
p249.en: Listen: If you only listen, there are few mistakes. At times, listening is the full treatment that people in difficult circumstances need. Its rationale is to encourage individuals to organize problems well enough to communicate. Therefore, those who speak out tend to come up with their own solutions. As an active listener, you can play a further role by providing feedback to each other: noding, maintaining an expression of interest, repeating each other's words and asking when you do not understand. As we have seen in the context of the visitors-centred therapy that we have seen before, it is interesting to listen actively to others and to share the same concerns (in the same way as others feel). At the same time, if you could avoid making suggestions, you would be better off, because they would deprive those who speak of the opportunity to come up with solutions themselves.

p250.original: 接纳：以来访者为中心的治疗师称之为非评判的态度。这意味着接受人和问题的本来面目，它还意味着抑制不利于解决问题并造成敌对气氛的震惊、厌恶或谴责。
p250.en: Admission: A visitor-centred therapist calls it a non-judgmental attitude. That means accepting the people and the nature of the problem, and it means suppressing the shock, disgust or condemnation that is not conducive to a solution and to a climate of hostility.

p251.original: 探索替代方案：当处于压力之下时，人们可能只会看到一种行动方案，因此你可以通过识别其他潜在选择并探索每种选择的结果来提供帮助（你可以指出什么都不做也是一种选择）。请记住，最终选择哪种行动不是由你决定，而是由拥有问题的人决定。
p251.en: Exploring alternatives: When under pressure, one may see only one course of action, so you can help by identifying other potential options and exploring the results of each option (you can say that doing nothing is an option). Remember that it is not up to you to choose which action is ultimately to be taken, but to the people who have the problem.

p252.original: 除了这些基本的帮助技巧之外，便是训练有素的治疗师的专业领域了。同样，我们强烈建议你不要尝试用本章中讨论的治疗技术来治疗抑郁症、恐怖症、焦虑症或DSM-5中列出的任何其他严重的心理障碍。
p252.en: In addition to these basic assistive techniques, it is the area of specialization of trained therapists. Likewise, we strongly recommend that you not try to treat depression, terror, anxiety or any other serious psychological disorder listed in the DSM-5 with the treatment techniques discussed in this chapter.
